thread:
anya: Heads up — bringing up Nimble-13B (converted from Gemma). int8 conversion looks stable performance-wise but we see token-level drift on some long-context QA and summarization tasks. Posting quick diffs + repros. :eyes:

sam: Can you drop the eval numbers and a minimal repro?

anya: Sure. Short eval snapshot (summarization / QA / instr-follow):
```
Llama-13B fp16 baseline:    ROUGE-L 37.1 | QA EM 72.3 | Instr 94.3
Nimble-13B int8 (converted): ROUGE-L 34.9 | QA EM 68.0 | Instr 87.8
Delta ~ -2.2 ROUGE-L, -4.3 EM, -6.5 instr
```

anya: Example failing prompt (QA):
"""
Context: <long doc clipped> ... note: the clause on page 7 says x.
Q: According to the doc, what is the threshold for x?
"""
Nimble returns a plausible but wrong sentence, Llama returns correct span.

anya: Repro commands:
```bash
python tools/convert_model.py --src-format gemma --dst-format nimble --in /models/gemma13b/ --out /tmp/nimble13b/ --permute-heads --tok-map ../token_maps/gemma->nimble.json
python infra/eval.py --model /tmp/nimble13b/int8 --tasks summarization,qa --batch 8 --max-len 2048
```

infra-bot: Scheduled: eval job 1759999999-ev completed on cluster-gpu-3 (runtime 22m) :white_check_mark:

clare: Two quick guesses: 1) rotary/base or freq scaling got changed during conversion; 2) token id offset (vocab mapping) introduced a shifted sentinel.

dave: +1 on token offset. I've seen off-by-one in tokenmaps when moving from byte-level vocab to different BPE merges. Quick check: run a small injection test to see if token ids for multi-byte punctuation match.

matt: Also try a KV-cache alignment test: mismatch in head ordering will cause model to prefer different attention patterns on long context. Run short->long context consistency.

anya: I ran a bisect: if I skip the `--permute-heads` flag the outputs line up with baseline. With `--permute-heads` we get the drift. So conversion is the suspect.

sam: Interesting. Could be headwise rotary mapping vs contiguous projection ordering. In our conversions we need to remap rotary params per-head if the projection dims are permuted. Try applying rotary with headwise freq calc rather than global.

clare: Quick diagnostic: cosine similarity between token embeddings at layer 0 for matched tokens:
```
baseline(fp16) vs nimble(int8 w/permute): 0.997, 0.991, 0.889 (tail samples)
```
Tail dropping to ~0.89 suggests either embedding remap or quantization bias after permutation.

dave: Tokenizer sanity check command: `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('vocab.json'); print(t.encode('—').ids)"` — compare across converted vocab and baseline. Also check for mapped id collisions.

matt: KV alignment check (quick):
```bash
python tests/kv_align.py --model /tmp/nimble13b/int8 --prompt-prefix-file tests/short_prefix.txt --extend 1024
```
Look at per-head cosine of cached keys across extension; if permuting, you'll see low correlation.

anya: Patch I used to temporarily fix: after load, reorder rotary tables to match projected head ordering and normalize freq scaling: `model.rotary.freq_scale = model.rotary.freq_scale.reshape(heads, -1)[perm]` — rough hack but it moves metrics back ~+1.2 ROUGE-L. Not a permanent solution.

sam: We should update conversion script to emit a `rotary_map.json` when `--permute-heads` is used, with mapping for head->proj slice. Also add a unit test that compares a few deterministic tokens across conversion.

clare: Another experiment: run quantization with preserved fp16 rotary tables (i.e., keep rotary params in fp16 while quantizing projections). That can isolate whether quantization step amplifies permute error.

anya: I tried that: keeping rotary fp16 recovers most of the instr-follow score (~ -1.4 gap vs baseline). So quantization amplifies the mismatch.

infra-bot: Note: created ticket #INF-4921 and attached conversion logs and eval artifacts.

matt: Action list:
- anya: push small conversion fix that emits rotary_map + unit test.
- matt: run KV alignment battery on Dedicated (mt-run) and post per-head plots.
- clare: run tokenization map audit and diff for multi-byte tokens.
- sam: schedule quantization sweep (fp16-rotary vs int8-rotary) on the small devset.

anya: I'll open PR for conversion fix today and attach repro case. Thanks all. :party_parrot:

sam: Nice triage. Once PR lands I'll kick off the quant sweep and then do an A/B against the Llama baseline on the long-doc QA set.

anya: FYI I'll also post a minimal reproducer gist and add to the model-onboarding checklist (step: emit rotary_map) after we land the fix.

clare: If anyone wants the raw eval artifacts I uploaded them to s3://redwood-dev/nimble13b/triage/1759999999/

anya: closing loop — will update here when PR merged and when infra-run completes.
